summary: id Software's foundational FPS series, including the classic IWADs, official expansions, mobile/VR spin-offs, modern reboot trilogy, and current Nightdive remasters.

entries.title: Doom

emulation.emulator: None for primary; DOSBox/source ports for historical play
emulation.notes: Use Doom + Doom II for the main archive route; preserve original IWADs for source-port study.

primary.why: The 2024 Doom + Doom II package is the definitive current route for the original Doom, bundling the classic game with modern KEX-engine features, official add-ons, mod support, cross-platform multiplayer, and the updated soundtrack.
primary.how_to_play: Play Doom through Doom + Doom II on Windows; use a source port only for historical/mod-specific compatibility after documenting the IWAD and add-on set.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document whether strict vanilla compatibility or modern KEX features are being used.

entries.title: Doom II: Hell on Earth

emulation.emulator: None for primary; DOSBox/source ports for historical play
emulation.notes: Use Doom + Doom II for the main archive route.

primary.why: The 2024 enhanced bundle includes Doom II, Master Levels, Final Doom content, No Rest for the Living, Sigil/Sigil II, Legacy of Rust, mod support, and cross-platform multiplayer.
primary.how_to_play: Play Doom II through Doom + Doom II on Windows, using the official game-selection menu for Master Levels and add-ons.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document strict vanilla/source-port needs separately from KEX enhanced play.

entries.title: Master Levels for Doom II

primary.why: The official Master Levels are now integrated into the Doom + Doom II menu, replacing the awkward original DOS launcher workflow.
primary.how_to_play: Launch Master Levels from Doom + Doom II on Windows and document the selected level order.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document whether using original WADs or integrated KEX menu.

entries.title: Final Doom

emulation.emulator: None for primary; DOSBox/source ports for original IWADs
emulation.notes: Use Doom + Doom II for main play.

primary.why: Doom + Doom II includes Final Doom's TNT: Evilution and The Plutonia Experiment, making Windows the most complete and convenient current route.
primary.how_to_play: Play TNT: Evilution and The Plutonia Experiment from Doom + Doom II on Windows.

entries.remaster_caveats: PlayStation Final Doom is a historically distinct version, not the complete TNT/Plutonia route.

entries.title: Doom 64

primary.why: The 2020 Nightdive remaster adds the Lost Levels expansion that connects classic Doom to the modern continuity, making Windows the best complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows remaster with The Lost Levels included; use Nintendo 64 only for original hardware study.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original N64 remains important for first-release preservation.

entries.title: Doom 3
entries.definitive_edition: BFG Edition on Windows for complete package; original Windows for original feel

primary.version: Doom 3: BFG Edition plus original-PC preservation
primary.why: BFG Edition bundles Doom 3, Resurrection of Evil, The Lost Mission, and classic Doom content, while the original PC release preserves the original flashlight/atmosphere balance; Windows supports both.
primary.how_to_play: Play BFG Edition on Windows for the complete official package, and keep the original PC release available if original atmosphere/mechanics matter.

entries.remaster_caveats: BFG Edition changes lighting/flashlight and balance feel; document which version is played.

entries.title: Doom 3: Resurrection of Evil

primary.why: Resurrection of Evil is bundled into Doom 3: BFG Edition and also exists as the original Windows expansion; Windows preserves both complete and original-expansion routes.
primary.how_to_play: Play through Doom 3: BFG Edition on Windows for the bundled route, or original Doom 3 plus expansion for original mechanics.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document whether using original expansion or BFG Edition.

entries.title: Doom RPG

primary.why: Doom RPG was released for Java ME and BREW mobile phones; preservation depends on a legally preserved mobile build and matching emulator/profile.
primary.how_to_play: Use a Java ME or BREW preservation emulator with a legally preserved build; document the phone/profile variant.

entries.remaster_caveats: No current official modern release is sourced.

entries.title: Doom Resurrection

primary.why: Doom Resurrection is an iOS-only rail shooter side story using Doom 3 assets.
primary.how_to_play: Preserve an old iOS install/device if available; document app version and device/OS.

entries.remaster_caveats: No current official modern release is sourced.

entries.title: Doom II RPG

emulation.emulator: iOS preservation / touchHLE-style compatibility if verified
emulation.notes: Document the exact build and compatibility route.

primary.why: Doom II RPG was released across Java ME, BlackBerry OS, Windows Mobile, and iOS; iOS is the best documented preservation route and can be preserved with old-device/touchHLE-style compatibility research.
primary.how_to_play: Use a preserved iOS build on original hardware or a verified compatibility layer; document app version and route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No current official modern release is sourced.

entries.title: Doom

primary.why: Doom (2016) shipped on PS4, Windows, Xbox One, Switch, and Stadia; Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows release through Steam/Game Pass/Bethesda-supported storefronts with patch and graphics settings documented.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document multiplayer/server state if preserving SnapMap or online features.

entries.title: Doom VFR

primary.why: Doom VFR is a VR spin-off on Windows VR and PlayStation VR; Windows VR is the highest-fidelity headset route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Windows with a compatible SteamVR headset and documented controller profile.

entries.remaster_caveats: Short VR side story; not a replacement for Doom (2016).

entries.title: Doom Eternal
entries.definitive_edition: Deluxe/current Windows release with The Ancient Gods

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows current build with ray tracing where supported

primary.version: Deluxe/current PC release with The Ancient Gods
primary.why: Windows supports the full campaign, Battlemode, ray-tracing PC update, and The Ancient Gods DLC with the broadest settings path.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows version with The Ancient Gods Part One and Part Two installed; document patch and graphics mode.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document Battlemode/server state and patch version.

entries.title: Mighty Doom

primary.why: Mighty Doom launched on Android and iOS but servers shut down on August 7, 2024, so Android is only a historical preservation target.
primary.how_to_play: No normal current play route; preserve installed client/media for documentation only.

entries.remaster_caveats: Discontinued service; no current normal play route.

entries.title: Doom: The Dark Ages

primary.why: The Dark Ages shipped day-and-date on Windows, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S; Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route for the current id Tech 8 game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows release through Steam, Xbox PC app/Game Pass, or another supported PC storefront; document patch, DLC, and graphics settings.

entries.remaster_caveats: Active modern title; revisit if major DLC or edition changes ship.
